title: Portrait of Frederick de Vries and His Dog

source.label: Cleveland Museum of Art: made in Haarlem, 1597

highlight.text: His portraits range in character from prints of the most minute hatching … to others of the greatest breadth of line-work, well exemplified in a portrait of himself

source.author: Arthur M. Hind
source.title: A Short History of Engraving and Etching

work.text: Goltzius made this print for his friend the painter Dirck de Vries (Netherlandish, active 1590–1609) to let him know how his son was progressing under Goltzius’s care in the Dutch city of Haarlem. The two artists had met in Venice, where de Vries still lived.

source.author: Cleveland Museum of Art
source.title: Portrait of Frederick de Vries and His Dog

work.text: His portraits, though mostly miniatures, are notable for their finish and characterization.

moment.text: Phidias, referred to in the inscription, was an ancient Greek sculptor whose works were celebrated for their classical forms and their expressions of noble and moral character.

source.author: Cleveland Museum of Art
source.title: Portrait of Frederick de Vries and His Dog

matters.text: I dedicate [this work] to the excellent painter Dirck de Vries in Venice out of friendship and to represent his absent son.
matters.lead: The inscription in the centre of the print:

source.author: Hendrick Goltzius
source.title: Dedication on Portrait of Frederick de Vries and His Dog (1597), translated by the Cleveland Museum of Art

matters.text: Simplicity seeks and loves faithfulness. The faithful dog and the innocent boy, that Goltzius faithfully rendered with a Phidian hand in copper.
